hooks.text: A zombie star survived its own supernova explosion.
Can a dying star survive its own supernova explosion?
One cosmic explosion failed to destroy its parent star.

title: The Star That Survived Its Own Supernova
description: In 1181, astronomers saw a supernova that should have destroyed a white dwarf. Instead, the star survived and today it screams through space blowing carbon-burning ashes.

beats.text: A zombie star survived its own supernova explosion.
beats.visual: artist concept of a white dwarf star surviving a supernova explosion

beats.text: Normally, these powerful runaway blasts completely obliterate a dying white dwarf star.
beats.visual: artist concept of a catastrophic type Ia supernova destroying a white dwarf

beats.text: But in the year 1181, astronomers witnessed a strange, rare cosmic blast in the night sky.
beats.visual: historical star chart showing the position of supernova 1181 in Cassiopeia

card.small: The Year of the Guest Star

beats.text: At the center of its remnant, IRAS 00500+6713, a bizarre zombie star survived.
beats.visual: Chandra X-ray Observatory image of the supernova remnant IRAS 00500+6713

beats.text: X-ray data from the XMM-Newton telescope recently revealed the trick behind this stellar miracle.
beats.visual: illustration of the ESA XMM-Newton space telescope orbiting Earth

beats.text: A carbon-oxygen white dwarf crashed directly into an oxygen-neon white dwarf.
beats.visual: illustration of two white dwarf stars merging and spiraling together

beats.text: This intense collision triggered a partial Type [Iax](/wˈʌnˈIˈɛks/) supernova instead of a total explosion.
beats.visual: artists concept of a weak Type Iax supernova explosion with surviving core

beats.text: Today, the surviving star WD J005311 continues screaming through space, blowing an intense stellar wind of carbon-burning ashes.
beats.visual: artists concept of white dwarf star WD J005311 blowing high-velocity winds

beats.text: This chaotic remnant proves that a star can actually outlive its own doom.
beats.visual: Chandra X-ray and optical composite image of the supernova remnant SN 1181

better_than_last: Refined the final beat to end with an evocative statement that flows seamlessly back into the hook's opening words.
